assessments.headline: Resinate Douglas — $48K, unowned, 59 days quiet
assessments.assessment: Six confirmed bulk orders in 2026, $48K, reordering every ~37 days — and nothing since July 28, three weeks past their rhythm. Last-90-day spend fell from $37K to $8K. Worcester (Joey, $26K, ordered Sept 11) is healthy; Douglas has no owner at all. Note: the Sheet had this store filed under BeWell — Resinate owns BeWell and the same buyers cover both, which is why it looked like a BeWell problem. BeWell Merrimac itself has one order this year.
assessments.action: Matt: give Douglas to Joey since he already has the Resinate relationship. Joey: one call to the Resinate buyers covers Douglas and Northampton (licensed, zero orders) — ask what changed on the Douglas bulk lots and quote the next one.

assessments.headline: $64K chain with no owner
assessments.assessment: Springfield ($36K) and Northampton ($28K) together are a top-5 relationship, reordering roughly every 10 weeks, last order 37 days ago. Both locations are Unassigned. A chain this size with no named rep is the biggest coverage gap in the book.
assessments.action: Matt: assign both locations to one owner. Owner: one call covers the chain — confirm the next order date and whether Worcester (licensed, zero orders) is a real third location to open.

assessments.headline: A+ account 22 days past its reorder
assessments.assessment: Eight orders, $38K, a tight 27-day cadence — and 49 days since the last one. Bulk & finished goods. This is Joey's account and it's the largest at-risk revenue he owns.
assessments.action: Joey: call this week, not email. Lead with a restock offer on whatever they bought most in August.

assessments.headline: Due for reorder in 3 days
assessments.assessment: Four orders averaging $5.3K on a 33-day rhythm; last order 30 days ago. Standing instruction: always include Lysah in Finance. Buyer is Nate Hall.
assessments.action: Joey: text Nate today with a menu — beat the reorder rather than chase it. Copy Lysah on the invoice.

assessments.headline: Chain due this week — one call covers three stores
assessments.assessment: Lowell and Gloucester are both due within 7 days (38-day rhythm, last order 31 days ago); Beverly ordered 10 days ago. Lowell's last-90-day spend is a third of the prior quarter — worth asking why. $82K across the three locations in 2026.
assessments.action: Joey: one call to the buyer for the chain — confirm Lowell and Gloucester reorders, and ask what shifted in Lowell.

assessments.headline: Growing fast, graded C
assessments.assessment: $28K in 2026, eight orders, and the last 90 days nearly doubled the prior quarter ($18K vs $9.5K). Still graded C and Unassigned — the grade is stale and the account has no owner.
assessments.action: Matt: regrade to A or B and assign an owner. Owner: ask what's driving the growth and whether Bourne (second license, tracked separately) is ready to order.

assessments.headline: Momentum account — expand the menu
assessments.assessment: #2 customer at $50K. Last 90 days ($27K) more than doubled the prior quarter. Ordered yesterday. Healthy 27-day cadence.
assessments.action: Joey: on the next visit, ask what they'd add if it were on the menu — this is where a new SKU lands first.

assessments.headline: #1 customer, healthy — protect it
assessments.assessment: $62K, ten orders, 27-day rhythm, last order 17 days ago. Nothing is wrong. That's exactly when accounts get taken for granted.
assessments.action: Joey: schedule a visit before the next reorder (~10 days) — check menu placement and in-store visibility rather than waiting for the order.

assessments.headline: Graded A, silent since April
assessments.assessment: Two orders, $12K, then nothing for 162 days. Unassigned. Either they churned or they're buying elsewhere; at Grade A the Sheet still thinks this is a priority account.
assessments.action: Owner: one honest call — 'we haven't heard from you since April, what happened?' Then regrade or reactivate.

assessments.headline: Both locations went dark on the same day
assessments.assessment: Westfield and West Springfield each ordered twice ($18K combined), last on May 27, then nothing for 121 days. Same-day stop across two stores is a decision, not drift — price, a competitor, or a buyer change.
assessments.action: Joey: find out which. If it's price, bring the tier discount; if it's a new buyer, start over with samples.

assessments.headline: Big first order, never came back
assessments.assessment: One $9.9K order in March on the January 15%-off COD promo, then 192 days of silence. Graded A. Classic promo buyer — the discount got the order, the product didn't get the reorder.
assessments.action: Joey: reopen with a visit and samples of what's moving now; don't lead with a discount.

assessments.headline: 34 days past reorder — the Sept 21 line was a placeholder
assessments.assessment: Four confirmed orders, $15K, a 36-day rhythm — and nothing since July 17. The tracker has a Sept 21 row for this store with no total and no status; that's a planned order, not a real one. Somerville is the same story: one real order in April, then a placeholder.
assessments.action: Joey: confirm whether the Sept 21 order actually happened. If it did, log it with the total; if not, this is a win-back call today.

assessments.headline: #5 customer, 12 days past its rhythm
assessments.assessment: Six confirmed orders, $36K, reordering every ~32 days — last real order Aug 12. The Sept 24 row in the tracker is a placeholder with no total. Graded B; this is A-tier revenue.
assessments.action: Joey: same as Fresh Connection — did the Sept 24 order ship? Log it or call. Matt: regrade to A.

assessments.headline: 11 tracker rows are placeholders, not orders
assessments.assessment: The bottom of the Order Tracker has 11 rows with a date and a store but no total and a blank status — Enlite (2), Fresh Connection (2), Ascend (2), Firehouse, Road Trip, Trinity, Thrive, Apex. The CRM now shows these as Planned and leaves them out of revenue and reorder math.
assessments.action: Whoever owns the tracker: when one of these ships, fill in the total and mark it Confirmed; if it fell through, delete the row. The CRM picks it up on the next refresh.

assessments.headline: 57 'Active' accounts have no 2026 orders
assessments.assessment: The Sheet marks 138 accounts Current, but 57 of them haven't ordered this year. They inflate the active count and hide the real base (~80 accounts driving $1.18M).
assessments.action: Matt: work the 'Active, no 2026 orders' list — move each to Pipeline or Non-prospect. A clean Active list is what makes the reorder alerts trustworthy.

assessments.headline: 197 accounts unassigned after Allen
assessments.assessment: Every account Allen owned is now Unassigned, alongside the ones that were never assigned. Joey owns 161. Until the book is split, quiet-customer alerts have nobody to land on.
assessments.action: Matt: bulk-assign from Active Accounts (select → assign). Start with the 15 unassigned accounts that ordered in 2026.

assessments.headline: 19 new CCC licensees, none claimed
assessments.assessment: 13 are in the Prospects pool and 6 already sit in the book. New licenses are the one lead source with a known open date — they're building menus right now.
assessments.action: Joey: claim five this week, intro call each, sample drop for any that bite.
